4.word_for_word: anurundhānāḥ — complying; accommodating themselves; acting in accordance
4.translation: ‘Anurundhānāḥ’ means complying, or acting in accordance.

5.word_for_word: dhāma — a portion or manifestation of power; kalā — a part; tat eva — that very; saptamaḥ garbhaḥ — seventh embryo; babhūva — became; kim tat dhāma — what was that manifestation of power; iti āha — he explains; yam anantam iti — with the words beginning ‘whom, Ananta’; harṣa-śoka-vivardhanaḥ — increasing joy and sorrow; ānanda-rūpasya — of him whose nature is bliss; avatīrṇatvāt — because of having descended; harṣaḥ — joy; pūrva-garbha-sādhāraṇa-dṛṣṭyā — from viewing him in the same way as the previous embryos; ca — and; śokaḥ — sorrow; iti — thus
5.translation: ‘Dhāma’ means a portion or manifestation of power; that very thing became the seventh embryo. What was that manifestation of power? He explains with the words beginning ‘whom, Ananta.’ He increased both joy and sorrow: joy because one whose nature is bliss had descended, and sorrow because he was viewed in the same way as the previous embryos.

7.word_for_word: nanu — but; sā — she; gokule — in Gokula; kim iti āste — why does she remain; ataḥ āha — therefore he says; anyāḥ ca iti — with ‘and other women’; na kevalam sā eva — not only she alone; anyāḥ api — but others also; iti — thus; vivareṣu — in secluded places; alakṣya-sthāneṣu — in places not visible
7.translation: But why does she remain in Gokula? Therefore he says, ‘and other women.’ It was not she alone, but others also. ‘In secluded places’ means in places that could not be seen.

8.word_for_word: jaṭhare — in the womb; santam — being; nanu — but; garbhaḥ — the embryo; ākṛṣyamāṇaḥ — while being drawn away; katham — how; jīvet — could live; ataḥ āha — therefore he says; māmakam dhāma — My own potency
8.translation: ‘Being in the womb.’ But how could the embryo live while being drawn away? Therefore He says, ‘My own potency.’
